summary: Burst of privileged API sessions originating from unusual .site domain after external transcription consent
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-12 08:45 and 2026-03-12 09:30 UTC we observed a rapid increase in privileged API sessions using a handful of service account tokens. Impact: potential unauthorized use of privileged endpoints (billing/usage and model-serving routes) for a narrow set of requests. Environment: production (us-east-1).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Identify affected service token in audit log. 2) Observe token exchange pattern (oauth callback) and origin IPs. 3) Recreate request flow using a test token to validate endpoint access pattern (do not reuse production tokens).
observed_signals: ~480 token-validated sessions in a 45-minute window for svc-transcriber@redwood-inference.com
Unusual user-agent string: 'TranscribeClient/1.0 (+https://transcribe.example.site)' seen in most entries
OAuth token exchange recorded against redirect_uri /oauth/transcribe/callback with referrer external-transcribe.example.site
logs: 2026-03-12T08:46:12Z audit: token=svc-transcriber id=abc123 path=/v1/streams status=200 ip=45.77.12.9 ua=TranscribeClient/1.0
comments: 2026-03-12 09:05 Aisha Patel: Initial detection from anomaly alert (auth-rate-spike). Confirmed high session volume tied to svc-transcriber service account.
2026-03-12 09:22 Nora Schmidt (SRE-oncall): Blocked IP range 45.77.0.0/16 at perimeter and added temporary WAF rule to rate-limit transcribe endpoints.
2026-03-12 09:40 Marcus Li (IAM): Rotated keys for svc-transcriber and disabled the OAuth client 'cli-78abc' pending investigation.
2026-03-13 11:15 Elena Ruiz (Security): Kicked off forensic capture of auth logs and requested an export of all OAuth callbacks for the prior 72h.
2026-03-14 07:30 Marcus Li: Created detection rule for 'unexpected client_id use' and added to prod-alerts channel. Follow-up: review legacy ingest tokens.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: A third-party transcription vendor's OAuth app was compromised, allowing silent consent flow and token exchange for a service account.
Hypothesis B: A developer reused a service account credential in an insecure environment; attackers scraped it via an exposed artifact. Less likely given IP/geolocation clustering.
Evidence: Redirects observed to external-transcribe.example.site with a token exchange pattern that matches the vendor's documented flow; vendor's DNS shows recent changes to cname records.
Forensics: Exported full oauth server logs, CloudTrail-like audit entries, and the sequence of IPs for correlation with external threat intel.
temporary_mitigation: Disabled the OAuth client 'cli-78abc', rotated svc-transcriber keys, forced immediate token revocation for active sessions, rate-limited transcribe endpoints, and applied WAF rule to block 45.77.0.0/16.
resolution: Work in progress: immediate mitigations applied (keys rotated, client disabled). Ongoing tasks: complete forensic analysis to determine if tokens were exfiltrated, audit all service accounts used by transcription workflows, notify vendor and request their incident report, and publish internal advisory. No confirmed data exfiltration to date; investigation remains open.
next_steps: 1) Complete forensic timeline and determine if tokens were ever exported. 2) Vendor engagement: request IOCs and review their client security. 3) Expand detection to catch similar client_id anomalies across prod regions. 4) Update runbook and schedule org-wide note about transient OAuth risks.
